passage:
An old hand-drawn map showed large trees that once lined a city street. Today, only three remained.
Students walked the street and compared the map with reality. They asked residents what had happened. Some trees were removed for roads, disease, or construction.
The class created a report suggesting where new trees could be planted without damaging pipes or sidewalks.
The old map became a guide for future greening.
Sometimes the past shows not only what was lost, but what might be rebuilt. A missing tree on a map can become a question for the present.
